newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 11.2 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate edged up to 11.2 percent from 10.4 percent on Monday amid shrinking demand and on short supply of kuna funds.
Daily trade was put at 22.2 million kuna, against the supply of 31 million.
Dealers said all borrowers' demands for loans were met, leaving a surplus of 9.2 million kuna at the end of trading.
Interbank rates ranged from 9.8 percent for call money and 13.8 percent for 31-366-day funds. Insurers charged 9.0 percent for short term loans.

Overnight trade over the weekend totalled 9.6 million kuna, as five banks with shortfalls demanded 2.6 million to square their positions. The rest went to other banks for maintenance of their reserve payments.
The central bank's exchange rate for Tuesday eased to 5.3956 against the dollar and to 3.5638 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
